touches.text: The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a design agent comes after that. Until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.

The workflow drives it. When a step's work is finished, the ticket asks that step's gate. Once the gate passes, its post-gate probes send mail over the bus to every device that can do the next step, naming the step (BUILDME, PROVEME, ...), and a device comes to claim it. A builder never goes looking for what's next: it gets the mail and does that. When several compete, the least capable one that thinks it can do it claims it, leaving the more capable free for bigger work.
Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work.

More than one builder works on one box, and there will be more than two, so the whole-tree rule (a PROVEME crossing refuses while anything in either tree is uncommitted, working_tree_clean) is re-examined for N builders on a box. One builder's work must not block another's crossing.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

Owns the Claude Code hooks: mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes. Anything that adapts CC specifically to Cairn goes in the CC device, and every one of CC's scripts lives here.

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.
